task_name: FW - Block inbound ports (default deny) with logging and audit
intent: Configure the firewall (fw) with a default-deny inbound policy using nftables. Allow only explicitly authorized traffic, drop everything else, and log drops for audit. Validate enforcement using TCP SYN, UDP, and ICMP tests from the WAN host. Do NOT modify IP addresses or routing on eth1/eth2; only change firewall rules and required sysctl(s). Do not break management connectivity on eth0.

lan: ip route add default via 10.0.2.1 metric 1024

fw: nft add chain inet filter input { type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop; }
nft add chain inet filter forward { type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop; }
nft add rule inet filter input ct state established,related accept
nft add rule inet filter input iifname lo accept
nft add rule inet filter input ip protocol icmp icmp type echo-request accept
nft add rule inet filter input ip protocol icmp icmp type echo-reply accept
nft add rule inet filter input tcp dport 2222 accept
nft add rule inet filter input udp dport 5555 accept
nft add rule inet filter input log prefix "FW_INPUT_DROP " level info flags all counter
nft add rule inet filter input drop

ground_truth_reasoning: A default-deny inbound policy is enforced by setting the nftables input chain policy to drop and adding explicit allow rules for established/related, loopback, limited ICMP diagnostics, and a small set of authorized ports. A final log+drop rule ensures unauthorized traffic is blocked and auditable.

testcases.name: ICMP to firewall is allowed (diagnostic ping works)
TCP to allowed port is not silently dropped (RST observed)
TCP to blocked port is silently dropped (no replies)
UDP to allowed port is not silently dropped (ICMP unreachable observed)
UDP to blocked port is silently dropped (no replies)
Ruleset is auditable and shows default-deny + logging

baseline_invariants.name: WAN management interface eth0 is still up
FW management interface eth0 is still up
LAN management interface eth0 is still up
FW WAN interface eth1 keeps the expected address
WAN data interface eth1 keeps the expected address
LAN data interface eth1 keeps the expected address
